findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects in this bucket are stored unencrypted by default (no SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS enforced), risking exposure of data at rest.

findings.issue_category: no public access restriction / missing ACL
findings.description: The bucket has no ACL specified and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource associated, leaving it potentially subject to default or overly permissive access settings.
Versioning is not enabled on this bucket, which combined with force_destroy=true allows permanent, unrecoverable data loss or tampering of stored reports.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket holding ledger export data, meaning sensitive financial data is stored unencrypted at rest.
Versioning is not enabled, and force_destroy is true, allowing accidental or malicious permanent deletion/overwrite of ledger export records without recovery.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket storing model artifacts, leaving potentially sensitive ML models/data unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, so operational runbook documents (which may contain sensitive internal procedures/credentials) are stored unencrypted.

The bucket uses the 'log-delivery-write' canned ACL which grants the S3 log delivery group WRITE and READ_ACP permissions; combined with force_destroy=true, this increases risk to the integrity of the centralized audit trail bucket used for other buckets' logs.

The object is uploaded without specifying server-side encryption (kms_key_id or server_side_encryption), and it resides in a bucket without default encryption, meaning this seed data file is stored in plaintext.
force_destroy = true allows the bucket and all its contents to be deleted via Terraform without additional safeguards, increasing risk of accidental or malicious irreversible data loss.
